clue.text: Early restriction on freedom of dramatist?

definitions.text: Early restriction on freedom of dramatist?

parts.words: Early restriction on freedom of dramatist?
parts.note: an enclosure where a toddler is kept safe restricts freedom early in life; read whimsically, it is a writer's tool belonging to a stage work

explanation.surface: A question about what first curbed a budding playwright's liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: The enclosure for a baby limits freedom early in life; split 4-3 it reads as the writing instrument of a drama, fitting a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fenced enclosure for infants is literally the first confinement a child meets.

clue.text: By Christmas, finally put single decoration on tree

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: the last letter of Christmas is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
the MM, Military Medal, is a British decoration
taken as written

explanation.surface: By Christmas, at last, hang a single bauble on the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoration' suggests a tree bauble but is a military medal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-fruited tree of the ebony family bears the Sharon fruit.

clue.text: Agreed to write a small volume with editors

parts.note: cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small volume
ED is an abbreviation for editor
the plural gives a second ED

explanation.surface: Consented to produce a slim book with help from editors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To write' links: write down the pieces. 'Volume' suggests a book but is a measure of space.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent or assent to a request is to accede.

clue.text: Mobile phone has bad name for producing strange effects

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters of phone move around
bad means wrong, so the letters of name come out wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A mobile phone with a bad name produces odd effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as one thing, but 'Mobile' rearranges PHONE into PHENO and 'bad' rearranges NAME into MENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable or unusual occurrences are called phenomena.

clue.text: New sailor's collars

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor; the 's gives AB'S

explanation.surface: A fresh mariner's neckbands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collars' looks like a noun but is a verb: arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab or collar a suspect both mean to grab or arrest them.

clue.text: The French crew in court creating a disturbance

indicators.note: the crew pieces sit inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A French ship's crew causing a ruckus in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant means loudly insistent or clamorous, i.e. making a noisy fuss.

clue.text: Driver getting round a disturbance amid applause

indicators.note: the disturbance pieces are placed in the middle of the applause word

parts.note: a cheer is applause
a riot is a disturbance

explanation.surface: A motorist getting round a fracas amid applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting round' are link words here; 'Driver' suggests a motorist but is one who drives a chariot.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drives a horse-drawn chariot.

clue.text: Garden pest reducible to a degree if one is removed

indicators.note: taking the one away leaves a degree, so building forward the one goes inside the degree

parts.note: a PhD is a doctoral degree
I is one

explanation.surface: A garden pest could be reduced to a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backward: remove I (one) from the answer and it reduces to A PHD, 'a degree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that attack plants.

clue.text: An obstruction to worker in firm

parts.note: a dam obstructs a river
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A barrier against a labourer in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but means unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Unyielding and resolute: someone immovable in their position.

clue.text: Attacks using hammers

definitions.meaning: to tilt at someone is to charge at them, as a jouster attacks with a lance
a tilt hammer is a heavy pivoted forge hammer, also called a tilt

explanation.surface: Assaults carried out with hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging with a lance is jousting, and pivoted forge hammers bear the same name.

clue.text: Neckwear provided by Belfast policeman?

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was the police force of Belfast and Northern Ireland
a policeman of that force is a 'RUC he', a male officer, so the man gives HE

explanation.surface: A collar or tie supplied by a Northern Irish constable.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC (Royal Ulster Constabulary) was the Northern Ireland police until 2001; a male officer is a RUC 'he', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered frill of fabric, traditionally worn as a decorative collar.

clue.text: Book every social occasion for seaside amusement

parts.note: every one means each
a ball is a formal dance, a social occasion

explanation.surface: Booking every party and outing for fun by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable toy thrown about on the sand is a classic holiday plaything.

clue.text: One can't be out, playing this sort of game

definitions.text: One can't be out, playing this sort of game

parts.words: One can't be out, playing this sort of game
parts.note: a game played under a roof keeps its players inside, so they cannot be outside; cricket's 'out' adds a sporting false trail

explanation.surface: A cricketer who cannot be dismissed in a certain kind of match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' suggests being dismissed in cricket, but it simply means outdoors: such games are played inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Games like darts or table tennis are played inside a building, never out in the open.

clue.text: Boring speakers deviate a lot

parts.note: a road that winds deviates from a straight course
bags of something means a lot of it

explanation.surface: Tedious orators wander off the point a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-winded, tiresome talkers are called gasbags or windbags in idiom.

clue.text: Friend in capital acquiring diamonds for Hannah, say

indicators.note: the capital piece takes the diamonds letter alongside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A friend in a big city picking up some diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannah' is a name that reads the same backward, so 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A word such as Hannah reads identically forwards and backwards.

clue.text: Insect's very small tail dropped off

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for very small is lost, as a tail is the end

parts.note: midget means tiny, very small

explanation.surface: A tiny creature has lost the end of its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat-like tiny fly is a familiar biting insect.

clue.text: Keeping tempo, adjust this highly regarded instrument

indicators.note: the word for adjust holds the tempo word inside it

parts.note: to alter is to adjust
tempo is musical time

explanation.surface: A musician adjusting a well-respected instrument while keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly regarded' looks like praise but means it regards height: the instrument measures altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft gauge reads how high it flies, so it literally regards heights.

clue.text: One friend includes another in intrigue

indicators.note: the first friend word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a mate is a friend
china, from rhyming slang china plate = mate, is another friend

explanation.surface: One friend brings another into a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so it means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or plot, to intrigue as a verb.

clue.text: Coming back up trail after near disaster

indicators.note: the trail piece comes after the rearranged piece
a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of near are rearranged

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: Climbing back up a path after a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back up' is the definition: renascent things rise again. 'Near disaster' looks like a narrow escape, but 'disaster' is the anagram signal working on 'near'.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or rising again, reviving.

clue.text: Bananas aren't nice — get this fruit instead

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Bananas are unpleasant, so choose a different fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like part of the fruit picture, but it signals an anagram of ARENT NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned peach variety is a stone fruit.

clue.text: Attracted by Church militant?

parts.note: armed means militant, ready to fight

explanation.surface: Drawn in by the Church militant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church militant is the Christian Church on earth, struggling against evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed means delighted or attracted, captivated.

clue.text: Complete egghead in family group

indicators.note: the head letter goes inside the family word

parts.note: a clan is a family group
the head of egg is its first letter E

explanation.surface: A brainy intellectual fits right into a family group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the head, first letter, of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean break or clean sweep is a complete, total one.

clue.text: English gamble, without doubt making a pile

indicators.note: without means outside, so the gamble word sits outside the doubt word

parts.note: to dice is to gamble
an if is a doubt or condition

explanation.surface: An English bet which, without doubt, makes a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'; 'a pile' suggests money, but means a grand building.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a large imposing building, as is an edifice.

clue.text: By the way, it is a furious attack with no leader

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, of the attack word is dropped

parts.note: a broadside is a fierce verbal or naval attack

explanation.surface: Incidentally, this is a ferocious assault without anyone leading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' poses as 'incidentally' but means beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated beside a road lies along the route, by the highway.

clue.text: Highland feature good to see during trip

indicators.note: the good letter is placed inside the trip word

parts.note: a ride is a trip

explanation.surface: A Scottish landscape sight worth seeing on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow raised stretch of land is a feature of high country.

clue.text: Commotion about a part of the flight

indicators.note: the commotion word goes round the a

parts.note: a stir is a commotion

explanation.surface: A fuss about part of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests a plane journey, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one unit of a staircase.

clue.text: Reduced text produced after taking skimpy notes

indicators.note: the text piece comes after the skimpy piece in the answer

parts.note: a mini skirt is skimpy, so mini means very small
MS, manuscript, is a text abbreviated or reduced

explanation.surface: A shortened text written from brief jottings.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-notes in music, each worth two crotchets, are musical notes.

clue.text: Bird settled in to feather nest

indicators.note: the bird is settled inside the words, lying within them

explanation.surface: A bird settles in to line its nest with feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Behaviour of humble old Sumerian city

parts.note: to humble someone is to demean them
Ur was an ancient city of Sumer

explanation.surface: Conduct typical of a lowly ancient Mesopotamian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner or bearing is how one conducts oneself outwardly.

clue.text: Burning with anger following return of note

indicators.note: the anger piece comes after the note piece
the musical note is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Seething with rage after a message came back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze means on fire, alight.

clue.text: Back Cockney's runner after tip

indicators.note: the runner piece follows the tip piece

parts.note: a tip is an end
a racehorse is a runner; a Cockney drops the H, saying 'orse

explanation.surface: Supporting a Londoner's racing tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, traditionally drop initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or vouch for a cause or person is to sign behind it.

clue.text: Head off from most taxing mountain

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the word for most taxing is removed

parts.note: severest means hardest, most taxing

explanation.surface: Beheaded on the hardest peak to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan peak is the world's highest.
